By stacking them, he can build towers of great height, and by placing the towers next to each other, he can create what he calls castles. However, he only likes castles that satisfy the condition that the number of blocks in a tower is always less than or equal to that of the tower immediately to its left. Additionally, he likes to describe these castles with a sequence of integers (ai)$$$(a_i)$$$ such that each ai$$$a_i$$$ corresponds to the number of blocks in the i$$$i$$$-th tower. After playing with this type of castle, he has realized that he can also describe them with a sequence (bi)$$$(b_i)$$$ such that each bi$$$b_i$$$ corresponds to the number of blocks on the i$$$i$$$-th floor of the castles. Given a castle described by the sequence (ai)$$$(a_i)$$$, determine the minimum number of blocks that need to be removed to convert it into a pretty castle.

output: For each case, print a single integer, the minimum number of blocks that need to be removed for the castle to be pretty.
